title: Factorization of a reflected square mate through its ambient mate
statement:
For $W\in\{S,T,X,Y\}$ let $\mathcal A_W$ be a category with a full reflective subcategory $\mathcal C_W$, reflector $C_W$ and unit $\kappa_W$; precomposition by $\kappa_{W,M}$ is a bijection on Hom into every object of $\mathcal C_W$. Suppose four adjunctions $L_f\dashv R_f$, $L_g\dashv R_g$, $L_h\dashv R_h$, $L_e\dashv R_e$ have directions $L_f:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal A_X$, $L_g:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal A_T$, $L_h:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_Y$, $L_e:\mathcal A_T\to\mathcal A_Y$, and each right adjoint preserves the full subcategories. Set $P_u=C_{\mathrm{source}(u)}L_u$ on the appropriate full subcategories and equip $P_u\dashv D_u=R_u|$ with the reflector/ordinary Hom bijection. Write $k_{u,M}=\kappa_{\mathrm{source}(u),L_uM}$. Suppose $\theta:L_hL_f\xrightarrow{\sim}L_eL_g$ and $\theta^c:P_hP_f\xrightarrow{\sim}P_eP_g$ are natural and satisfy, for $M\in\mathcal C_S$,
$$\theta^c_M k_{h,P_fM}L_h(k_{f,M})=k_{e,P_gM}L_e(k_{g,M})\theta_M.$$
For $K\in\mathcal C_T$ let $b_K:L_fR_gK\to R_hL_eK$ be the ordinary mate of $\theta$, and let $\alpha_K:P_fD_gK\to D_hP_eK$ be the completed mate of $\theta^c$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Then
$$\alpha_K k_{f,D_gK}=R_h(k_{e,K})b_K.$$
This equation is natural in $K$ and uniquely determines $\alpha_K$ among maps $P_fD_gK\to D_hP_eK$. Equivalently its ordinary $L_h\dashv R_h$ transpose is $k_{e,K}L_e(\varepsilon_{g,K})\theta_{R_gK}$. The target $R_hP_eK$ lies in $\mathcal C_X$, so the uniqueness uses the reflector Hom bijection at $L_fR_gK$. No assertion that either mate is invertible is included.

mathlib_searches.query: In a square of adjunctions with reflective subcategories the completed mate after the completion unit equals the ambient mate followed by completion and right adjoint
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: unit_mateEquiv, mateEquiv_counit and mateEquiv_square are genuine ingredients for abstract mates. They do not themselves construct the reflected adjunctions or replace the two completed counits and four completion units in this equation. Combining their formulas with the noninvertible reflector units is the extracted argument.
